about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

cotton.fundamental: Still no fresh supply or demand data in the shortened session; old-crop Mar holds just under its 83.4 resistance while crude turns lower intraday, removing part of the outside support. Certificated stock flows remain the thing to watch for longs.
events: Cotton rallies out of the Thanksgiving break (Barchart)
WTI reverses to ~82.8 (-1.9%) as Iraq lifts exports (OilPrice)

sugar.fundamental: The real's jump on the Trabuco appointment is the dominant input: a stronger real raises the dollar break-even for Centre-South mills and discourages new forward hedges, a modest prop for prices while the Brazilian intercrop season starts. Crude's intraday reversal trims the ethanol-parity support a little.
events: Real holds ~5.50/USD after Trabuco agrees to run the finance ministry (Reuters)
WTI back near 82.8 on higher Iraqi exports (OilPrice)

coffee.fundamental: Brazil's record but quality-mixed harvest keeps the flow of new arabica toward ICE warehouses as the key bearish risk, while certified stocks near historic lows still support the nearby; the firmer real slows grower selling at the margin. No new cert or Antwerp figures over the holiday.
events: Record Brazil crop carries quality and stock questions (Daily Coffee News)

cocoa.fundamental: No new Ivorian port-arrival or Ghana COCOBOD figures this week; reports that the delayed Ivorian crop may bunch up at ports before EU deforestation rules apply point to slow near-term flow but heavier supply later. ICCO's November bulletin is not out yet.
events: Delayed Ivorian crop could congest ports ahead of EUDR (Reuters via Nation Africa)
